MIND. [1] [Bapt.]
Unconsciousness. θ Typhus.
Stupor ; falls asleep while being spoken to, or answering ; heavy sleep until aroused ; awakes only to again fall asleep in the midst of his answer, which he vainly endeavors to finish. θ Typhus.
Confusion of ideas ; confused as if drunk.
Cannot confine his mind ; a sort of wild, wandering feeling.
Cannot go to sleep, because he cannot get himself together. θ Orchitis. θ Typhoid.
Sensation as if there was a second self outside of patient. θ Typhus.
Feels scattered about, and tosses about to get the pieces together. θ Typhus.
He thinks his gouty legs are holding a conversation with each other ; a man, æt. 60. θ Gout.
He thinks his toe is holding a confab with his gouty thumb.
Delirium, especially at night, or constant, low ; stupor. θ Typhus.
Delirium and incoherent talk. θ Typhus.
Delirious stupor or fierce delirium. θ Typhus.
Low muttering. θ Typhus.
Indisposed to think, want of power ; mind seems weak.
Aversion to mental or bodily exertion, or to hear conversation about sickness or injuries ; feeble mind ; fretful. θ Spasmodic stricture of œsophagus.
Hopeless of recovery, and certain of death. θ Typhus.
Mentally restless, but too lifeless to move.
Restless and delirious for three weeks. θ Typhus.
Want of mental force. θ Typhus.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Bapt.]
Vertigo and weak feeling of entire system, especially of lower limbs and knees.
Giddiness and severe nausea. θ Typhus.
Dull, heavy sensation in head with drowsiness ; unfit for mental labor.
Frequent fainting ; tongue dry, brown, in morning.
   

INNER HEAD. [3] [Bapt.]
Peculiar feeling in head, which is never felt except during fever, excitement of brain, such as precedes delirium.
Head feels large and heavy, with numb feeling of head and face ; stitches or shocks in various parts of head.
Frontal headache, weighty. θ Typhus.
Frontal headache : with pressure at root of nose ; with feeling of fulness and tightness of whole head.
Sharp darts of pain in supraorbital nerve at foramen.
Dull bruised ache in head. θ Typhus.
Dull, bruised feeling in occiput. θ Diphtheria.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Bapt.]
Dull, bruised ache in head. θ Typhus.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Bapt.]
Cannot bear light ; eyes burn, but do not water. θ Chronic sore eyes.
Occasionally delirium with confusion of sight. θ Diphtheria.
Feeling as if eyes would be pressed into head ; eyeballs feel sore with great confusion of sight ; cannot place anything, until after looking at it a few seconds ; everything appears to move.
Eyes dull. θ Typhus.
Weight over eyes. θ Typhus.
Eyeballs feel sore ; sore and lame on moving them.
Chronic sore eyes.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Bapt.]
Dull hearing. θ Typhus.
Delirium with almost complete deafness. θ Diphtheria.
Soreness in right ear, running down neck.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Bapt.]
Dull pain at root of nose. θ Catarrh.
Epistaxis and oozing of dark blood from nose for two or three days. θ Typhus.
Sensation of great fulness, œdematous swelling of affected parts, especially in choanæ. θ Diphtheria.
   

UPPER FACE. [8] [Bapt.]
Looked ill for two weeks. θ Typhus.
Anxious, frightened look. θ Cough.
Yellowish cheeks ; central deep flush. θ Typhus.
Face : sallow ; dark red, with besotted expression ; flushed, dusky ; hot and perceptibly flushed.
Burning heat in face with flushed cheeks. θ Diphtheria.
Cheeks flushed, dark violet. θ Cough.
Heat all over, most in face. θ Typhus.
Critical sweat on forehead and face. θ Typhus.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Bapt.]
Pain in articulation of lower jaw. θ Typhus.
Jaw dropped. θ Typhus.
Cracked lips, with bleeding and ulceration of bowels. θ Typhus.
   

TEETH AND GUMS. [10] [Bapt.]
Teeth and gums sore ; by pressing with finger large quantities of blood ooze out.
Sordes on teeth and lips ; tongue ulcerated. θ Typhus.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Bapt.]
Foul or bitter nauseous taste in mouth. θ Typhus.
Tongue swollen, thick, making talking difficult.
Tongue red and dry in middle. θ Typhus.
The roof of tongue is swollen and feels numb. θ Diphtheria.
Tongue of a dark hue. θ Cough.
Dry, parched, thickly coated tongue. θ Typhus.
Tongue dry, brown down centre. θ Typhus.
Tongue covered with a thick, brown crust. θ Typhus.
Tongue baked down centre. θ Typhus.
Tongue at first white with red papillæ here and there, followed by a yellow-brown coating in centre, edges being red, shining.
Tongue coated white, yellow or yellowish-brown, and feels as if burned or scalded. θ Diphtheria.
Tongue yellowish-white, deeply furred. θ Typhus.
Tongue has a yellow centre, or yellowish-brown coating, dry. θ Typhus.
Foul tongue. θ Typhus.
Cracked, sore, ulcerated tongue. θ Typhus.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Bapt.]
Stomatitis materna ; breath fetid ; feeble state.
Fetid odor ; also after mercury.
Mouth and tongue very dry. θ In fevers.
Cancrum oris, copious saliva ; gums loose, flabby, dark red, or purple ; fetid.
Aphthæ. θ Typhus.
Sore mouth of sucklings and consumptives.
Canker sores in mouth.
Ulcerations extending from mouth, through alimentary canal, with watery discharges from bowels.
Putrid ulceration of buccal cavity, with salivation ; well-developed ulcers, slight pain.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Bapt.]
Pain and soreness of fauces. θ Diphtheria.
Fauces dark red ; dark, putrid ulcers ; tonsils and parotids swollen ; unusual absence of pain. θ Diphtheria. θ Putrid sore throat, etc. θ Typhus. θ Variola.
Tonsils and soft palate swollen, with constant inclination to swallow, not accompanied by pain. θ Diphtheria.
Tonsils and soft palate very red, but not painful.
Tickling in throat provoking cough ; uvula elongated.
Sore throat.
Throat sore ; averse to open air.
Mucus rattles in throat. θ Typhus.
Œsophagus feels as if constricted from above down to stomach ; can only swallow water.
Constrictive feeling causing frequent efforts at deglutition ; throat sore, feels contracted.
Throat feels swollen, full ; tonsils and soft palate congested ; frequent inclination to swallow, causing pain in root of tongue.
Spits out liquids put in mouth. θ Typhus.
Can swallow liquids only ; least solid food gags. θ Spasmodic stricture of œsophagus. θ Diarrhœa.
Children cannot swallow solid food ; the smallest solid substance causes gagging, thus they cannot use anything but milk ; sometimes thin, watery, offensive passages day and night. (Compare Silicea).
Unable to swallow. θ Typhus.
Paralysis of organs of deglutition. θ Typhus.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Bapt.]
Loss of appetite. θ Typhus.
Constant desire for water, with nausea and want of appetite. θ Typhus.
Great thirst. θ Typhus.
A good deal of thirst. θ Typhus.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Bapt.]
Feels as if she wants to raise a great deal.
Retching and vomiting. θ Typhoid fever.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Bapt.]
Sinking, "gone" feeling at stomach, fainting ; tongue brown in morning. θ Dyspepsia after typhus.
Sinking sensation in stomach. θ Typhus.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Bapt.]
Constant pain in stomach and liver ; < walking ; hot sensation ; heavy aching in stomach and liver.
Pain in liver, from right lateral ligament to gall-bladder ; can scarcely walk, it so augments pain in gall-bladder.
Must stir about, yet motion is painful ; pain over gall-bladder.
Constant aching distress in stomach and umbilical region, with a great deal of pain in region of gall-bladder ; pain extends to spine.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Bapt.]
Pain in abdomen with diarrhœa. θ Typhus.
Distress, dull pain in umbilical region.
Right iliac region sensitive. θ Typhus.
Abdominal muscles sore on pressure, with acute intermitting pain. θ Typhus.
Abdominal tenderness, with flatulency ; 10th day. θ Typhus.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Bapt.]
Diarrhœa, with pain and soreness in bowels. θ Typhus.
Soft, papescent stool, with large quantities of mucus.
Fetid, exhausting diarrhœa, causing excoriation.
Aphthous diarrhœa.
Involuntary diarrhœa ; 9th to 11th day. θ Typhus.
Evacuation light yellow or brown, thin and watery. θ Typhus.
Dark brown mucous and bloody stools, with typhoid tendency ; brown tongue, etc.
Stools : dark, thin, fecal, offensive.
Fetid stools. θ Typhus.
Dysentery : rigors, pains in limbs and small of back ; stools small, all blood, not very dark, but thick ; great tenesmus ; great prostration, brown tongue, low fever ; in the Autumn, or in hot weather.
Colicky pains before stool. θ Dysentery in old people.
Constipation and diarrhœa ; stools dark and bloodstreaked. θ Diphtheria.
Stricture from piles.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Bapt.]
Urine very highly colored and scanty. θ Typhus.
Urine alkaline, fetid. θ Typhus.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Bapt.]
Orchitis ; cannot sleep because he feels as if his body was scattered about bed.
   

PREGNANCY. PARTURITION. LACTATION. [24] [Bapt.]
Threatened abortion. θ Typhus.
Lochia acrid, fetid ; great prostration.
Puerperal fever, with typhoid symptoms.
Stomatitis materna.
   

VOICE AND LARYNX. TRACHEA AND BRONCHIA. [25] [Bapt.]
Aphonia. θ Diphtheria.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Bapt.]
Fetid breath. θ Typhus.
Awoke with great difficulty of breathing ; lungs felt tight, compressed ; could not get a full breath ; must open window and get his face to fresh air ; burning heat of skin ; dry tongue ; accelerated pulse ; peculiar feeling of brain.
On lying down difficult breathing, but no constriction of chest, must rise ; afraid to go to sleep, fears nightmare and suffocation ; arises from want of power in lungs, not constriction.
Dyspnœa, with a tight cough.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Bapt.]
Pulse 100-125, hard in evening. θ Typhus.
Pulse 110, variable, weak, thready. θ Typhus.
Pulse small and quickened. θ Typhus.
Pulse 100 and feeble. θ Typhus.
Pulse 120 and thready.
Pulse 120, small and weak. θ Cough.
Pulse accelerated or slower than in health. θ Diphtheria.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Bapt.]
Neck so tired she cannot hold her head easy in any position ; sore down neck.
Catarrhal pneumonia ; elevated temperature ; pulse over a hundred, even with excessive cough and hemorrhages ; cavities ; night sweat and diarrhœa (relieves greatly).
Dull lumbar backache, worse walking.
Feels as if lying on a board ; changes position often, bed feels so hard ; worst part in region of sacrum. θ Typhus.
Pain in sacrum. θ Typhus.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Bapt.]
Left foot numb, prickling.
Burning of top of right foot, from toes to back of foot.
   

NERVES. [36] [Bapt.]
Restlessness. θ Typhus.
Morbid irritability of nervous system, preventing sleep. θ Typhus.
Restless, uneasy, could confine himself to nothing ; wanted to be moving from place to place, evening. θ Typhus.
General malaise for several days. θ Typhus.
General weak feeling, but especially of lower limbs.
Feels weak, tremulous, as if recovering from sickness, and yet incapable of vigorous mental or physical exertion.
Entire system feels weak, especially lower limbs and knees ; vertigo.
Faintness on rising. θ Typhus.
Great languor ; wants to lie down.
Great prostration and restlessness. θ Cough.
Prostration and trembling. θ Typhus.
Prostration. θ Diphtheria.
Disagreeable prostration, with soreness of muscles. θ Typhus.
Slides down in bed ; feels as if sinking away. θ Typhus.
Lay in semiconscious condition when she appeared dying. θ Typhus.
Paralysis of whole left side ; left hand and arm are numb, powerless.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Bapt.]
Excessive drowsiness.
Drowsy, stupid, tired feeling ; disposition to half close eyes.
Delirious stupor : falls asleep while answering a question or while being talked to.
Lies semicomatose, looks as if dying. θ Typhus.
Slept well until about 3 A. M., then restless until morning, tossing about.
Restless ; does not sleep quietly.
Wants to get up and yet does not want to. θ Typhus.
Sleepless, with wandering of mind. θ Typhus.
Delirious disturbance at night, varying from a mere uneasiness and inability to sleep to delirium proper. θ Typhus.
Cannot sleep ; head or body feels scattered about bed ; tosses about to get pieces together. θ Typhus and other diseases.
Wants to get out of bed. θ Typhus.
Restless, with frightful dreams. θ Typhus.
Sleeplessness. θ Typhus.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Bapt.]
Great aversion to open air. θ Spasmodic stricture of œsophagus.
Chilled by standing in cold wind ; fever returned, with rapid prostration. θ Typhus.
   

FEVER. [40] [Bapt.]
Shivering. θ Typhus.
Shivering preceded by a sense of weakness. θ Typhus.
Chilly all day ; whole body feels sore.
Chilly on going into open air ; chills over back and lower limbs ; evening.
Chilliness alternated with heat. θ Typhus.
Chilliness of lower limbs and back, with fever at night. θ Diphtheria.
Chill followed by fever, with severe aching in muscular portion of body. θ Typhus.
Whole surface hot and dry, with occasional chills, mostly up and down back.
Gentle flashes of heat over whole body.
Fever set in with headache. θ Typhus.
General fever and malaise.
Heat of face, flashes over face.
Burning, pungent heat over whole body, especially in face. θ Typhus.
Heat of skin. θ Typhus.
Frequent sweats. θ Typhus.
Causes sweat to break out and relieves ; critical sweat on forehead and face. θ Typhus.
Fetid sweat.
Fever cases, with peculiar delirium ; dulness of intellect and abdominal tenderness.
Sensation as if there was a second self outside of patient. θ Typhus.
Fever, delirium, headache, pain in back and limbs ; (compare Rhus). θ Typhus.
General fever and malaise. θ Typhus.
Aspect of low fever. θ Typhus.
Determination of blood to surface and profuse sweating. θ Typhus.
Early stages : white tongue, red edges ; or brown, or yellow brown down centre ; bitter or flat taste ; cannot digest food ; stools frequent, yellow ; gurgling and slight sensitiveness of right iliac region ; pulse high ; fever tends to increase ; parts rested on are sore. θ Typhus.
Typhus and typhoid fever, with a tendency to putrescence.
Fever originating from confinement on shipboard, without good care or food.
Beginning of typhus, when so-called nervous symptoms predominate.
Cerebral forms, especially with excessive drowsiness, delirium, confusion of ideas, stupefying headache ; restless sleep, head feels scattered about ; frightful dreams ; great debility and nervous prostration, with erethism, etc.
Typhoid and cerebral forms of fever ; delirium, drowsiness, confusion, gives slow answer or falls asleep attempting a reply ; erethism ; tries to escape from bed ; sleepless because she cannot get herself together ; head feels scattered, and she tosses about to get pieces together ; sensation of a second self outside of patient ; indifferent ; low delirium, stupor ; sordes on teeth ; face dark, besotted looking ; hearing dull ; epistaxis ; involuntary, scanty stool ; difficult breathing ; fever increases each afternoon.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Bapt.]
Prostration with disposition of fluids to decompose.
Discharges and exhalations fetid ; breath, stools, urine, sweat, ulcers.
Ulceration of mucous membranes, especially those of mouth ; also with tendency to putrescence.
Enlarged glands.
Diseases of mucous membranes.
Derangements of mucous surfaces, generally with vomiting and purging.
   

SKIN. [46] [Bapt.]
Rose-colored spots on 9th day. θ Typhus.
Pimples thick on palatine arch, tonsils and uvula ; breath fetid ; salivation ; prostration. θ Variola.
Foul, gangrenous, phagedenic syphilitic sores.
Smallpox confluent, tardy eruption.
Gangrenous sores, aphthæ, sore nipples (locally).
